answer: Proof-of-unique-latency registration: a registry sends each applicant a random challenge every pulse, a ten-minute window, and demands a signed reply from a physically distinct network location. Three independent verifier nodes measure round-trip times and compare them with the claimed region. Keys whose timing profiles overlap, as with one falcon-rack server hosting many clones, are merged into one slot. A new identity needs its own rented host and IP block, costing an attacker about six dollars monthly in copper-line hosting fees per fake.
